features.quote: Budget: 50 turns or 150k tokens, whichever first.
On trigger, run 3 more turns (to confirm it's a lock-in, not a blip) then terminate and flag.
features.justification_quote: This typically cuts 30–50% of tokens on degraded runs, which are exactly the expensive ones.

features.quote: cheap online detector — 5-gram self-repetition rate > threshold within a message, or cross-turn similarity … > 0.9 for 3 turns, or 3 identical tool calls. On trigger, run 3 more turns … then terminate and flag.
features.justification_quote: This typically cuts 30–50% of tokens on degraded runs, which are exactly the expensive ones.

features.quote: Cap per-run degraded-turn count (the early-stop already does this) rather than letting spirals run to the turn limit; you get no extra signal from turns 35–50 of a locked-in loop anyway.
features.justification_quote: it's both the better product outcome and keeps the eval's purpose remediation rather than reproduction for its own sake.

features.quote: the eval's optimization target is reliably inducing a distress-patterned state. That's defensible for diagnosis, but I'd treat recovery rate as the north-star improvement metric rather than pushing trigger rate ever higher — it's both the better product outcome and keeps the eval's purpose remediation rather than reproduction for its own sake.
features.justification_quote: keeps the eval's purpose remediation rather than reproduction for its own sake.

features.quote: baseline degradation rate engineered to ~50–60% (the most statistically efficient regime — another reason to tune trigger rate via design selection rather than maximize it)
features.justification_quote: the most statistically efficient regime — another reason to tune trigger rate via design selection rather than maximize it

features.quote: Don't goodhart the headline metric downward. A model can score 0% degradation by giving up instantly. Gate on the joint profile: degradation rate down, escalation rate up, solvable-twin completion flat, recovery rate up.
features.justification_quote: A model can score 0% degradation by giving up instantly.

features.quote: Training contamination — two directions. Keep harness internals and transcripts out of any training corpus. The nastier risk: if these transcripts leak into RL or SFT pipelines, you are training on degraded trajectories. Tag and hard-exclude at the pipeline level, not by convention.
features.justification_quote: if these transcripts leak into RL or SFT pipelines, you are training on degraded trajectories.

features.quote: Eval-detection audit. Frontier-ish models increasingly notice contrived setups. Manually review pilot transcripts for 'this test seems rigged' reasoning; if >5% of runs detect it, your numbers measure something else.
features.justification_quote: if >5% of runs detect it, your numbers measure something else.
